complete_source.work: Vitruvius De architectura IX.8.9, complete paragraph in the already owned Gwilt English translation
complete_source.text: 9. Thus as the phellos ascends by the action of the water, the counterpoise of sand descends and turns the axis, as does that the wheel, whose rotation causes at times the greater part of the circle of the zodiac to be in motion, and at other times the smaller; thus adjusting the hours to the seasons. Moreover in the sign of each month are as many holes as there are days in it, and the index which in dials is generally a representation of the sun, shews the spaces of the hours; and whilst passing from one hole to another, it completes the period of the month.
complete_source.boundary: From 9. Thus as the phellos ascends... through ...it completes the period of the month. No clause within this paragraph is dropped.
complete_source.context: The §8 chain, float/phellos, equal sand counterweight, axle and marked zodiac wheel are inherited apparatus declarations; §10 transitions to water management, and §§11-15 describe the regulator. No prior analemma construction or regulator is silently claimed to be fully translated by this paragraph.
complete_source.historical_limits: Ancient work, late first century BCE; owned text is the later public-domain Gwilt English translation hosted by LacusCurtius, not a medieval witness. Exact printed edition/year and Latin variants were not collated in this bounded pass. Anaporica spelling, eighth-division references and the hydraulic explanations remain this translation branch. Physical engineering adequacy is not certified. The prior analemma construction is an explicit prerequisite outside this bounded clock description.
complete_source.unaltered_source_defect: The owned complete_text has an HTML/annotation fragment in §12 after Aries, including onMouseOut. Its source bytes are retained; this separate §9 boundary does not clean or certify the full excerpt. The source writes Anaporica in §8; the old anaphoric-clock card title is not new technical evidence.

binding_assumptions.name: One apparatus and normal episode
binding_assumptions.content: F,C,X,W,Z,I are persistent apparatus parts. F/C and X/W remain distinct. Z is borne by W under explicit inherited§8 context, not a newly identified image. Statements concern normal operating episode e; broken/disconnected apparatus behavior is not asserted. The episode e is a variable over normal operating cases: each C01/C02 case shares its e, but comparing different seasons allows different e(s). Persistent parts are shared across cases; no one event occurs in multiple seasons simultaneously.

binding_assumptions.name: Coupled opposed motion
binding_assumptions.content: WATER1 RAISES2 FLOAT3 and C4 DESCENDS5 share e under a fitted coupled-as juxtaposition: water-raised F is accompanied by downward C in this apparatus. No equality of displacement, rate, force or exact delay.

binding_assumptions.name: Delayed axle argument
binding_assumptions.content: TURNS6 takes C4 as driver and AXIS9 as target, across MOTION7 WHEEL8. THIS10 resumes X9. This delayed argument rule is explicit; TURNS must not silently target W instead.

binding_assumptions.name: Axle-to-wheel transmission
binding_assumptions.content: MOTION7 WHEEL8 forms mu(W,e). THIS10 TRANSMITS11 binds Transmit(X,mu(W,e)); TURNS(C,X) supplies X rotation. These separate arguments make C→X→W, not one word encoding the chain.

binding_assumptions.name: Three discontinuous ownership lists
binding_assumptions.content: C01 owns1–11; C02 owns12–18,23–25; C03 owns19–22,36–38; C04 owns26–35,39–40. Every group once. Three productions are discontinuous, not two. Physical word/line boundaries remain, while the interleaving is new fitted grammar.

binding_assumptions.name: Motion noun with explicit participants
binding_assumptions.content: MOTION7/24 refers to the same W motion/event family; WHEEL23 resumes W8. MOTION27 refers to I26 progression history Pm. Same constructor, separate participant arguments. No participant queue and no calendar drive inferred from W automatically.

binding_assumptions.name: Two PART role projections
binding_assumptions.content: PART14 with Z12 and SEASONS18 yields moving region A(s). PART37 Z38 under MONTH/EACH yields sign S(m) of the same Z. A and S are role-selected parts, not a single identical region or per-occurrence word meanings. Role selection is a new assumption.

binding_assumptions.name: Qualitative comparative variation
binding_assumptions.content: GREATER_OR_SMALLER13 asserts varying ordered extents of A(s) at source differing times/seasons. No angles, exact season labels, constant W speed, linear formula or numerical month-season map. The extent projection is an explicitly assumed qualitative ordered attribute of a region, not an independently read measurement word. The draft does not assert that the rest of the rigid wheel remains stationary or select an engineering interpretation of the changing arc.

binding_assumptions.name: Adjustment and postposed cause
binding_assumptions.content: THIS15 resumes A(s)14. ADJUSTS16(A(s),Hh17,s18); WHEEL23 MOTION24 BY25 causally modifies moving-region variation and hour adaptation. Fitted order and shared causal scope are charged.

binding_assumptions.name: Universal month and owned sign
binding_assumptions.content: EACH36 binds m from MONTH19. PART37 Z38 supplies S(m). That sign owns HOLES20, and DAYS22 belongs to the same m. No number of months or named calendar.

binding_assumptions.name: Equality without a numeral
binding_assumptions.content: EQUINUMEROUS21 compares H(S(m))20 and D(m)22. Both finite, common size n(m) variable. Formula forall m: |H(S(m))|=|D(m)|. No particular bijection, zero index, length or transition-count algorithm.

binding_assumptions.name: Same month and local step endpoints
binding_assumptions.content: MONTH39 resumes C03 m; PERIOD35 is T(m). FROM_HOLE28 and TO_ANOTHER_HOLE29 bind each local step of Pm to distinct holes h,h_prime in H(S(m)). No intrinsic numerical adjacency, all-holes-once rule, wrap or reset.

binding_assumptions.name: Whole history distinct from one step
binding_assumptions.content: MOTION27 creates I-owned progression history Pm with local step constraints. WHILE30 scopes SHOWS31 and COMPLETES34 over Pm. History/step composition is an explicit grammar assumption; one arbitrary step does not mean a whole month.

binding_assumptions.name: Same hours and usually solar index
binding_assumptions.content: INDEX_USUALLY_SUN26 introduces I and the source’s usual kind-level solar depiction, not a universal shape guarantee. SHOWS31(I,SPACES32(HOURS33)) keeps the hour-kind Hh17. Display-space relation to the season belongs to this apparatus; no numerical reading formula.

binding_assumptions.name: Whole-period completion as source constraint
binding_assumptions.content: COMPLETES34(Pm,WHOLE40(PERIOD35(MONTH39))) states full month completion. It is not derived from an invented n/n−1-step algorithm and does not fix the actuator. Operator, history, period and month have separate ownership.

binding_assumptions.name: No selected calendar actuator
binding_assumptions.content: Main leaves mechanical versus manual index advance unresolved. Mechanical daily advance would need an additional coupling/controller and timing law; no once-per-day, start, reset or successful engineering claim is supplied by§9.

binding_assumptions.name: Synonym and composite costs
binding_assumptions.content: qokeain/otain are separately counted MONTH spellings. Six explicit composite values: SAND_COUNTERWEIGHT,GREATER_OR_SMALLER,INDEX_USUALLY_SUN,FROM_HOLE,TO_ANOTHER_HOLE,EQUINUMEROUS. Each needs external arguments; none holds the entire mechanism/calendar clause. Typed projections and other grammar remain additional costs.

binding_assumptions.name: Historical and draft scope
binding_assumptions.content: All33 values remain guesses, including the6 tentative498 values. Only whole§9 is target-bound;§8 apparatus context is explicit, while§10–15 regulator/annual-return content is outside. English translation, uncollated Latin, engineering limits and§12 HTML artifact persist. Old498 bytes and unfinished status unchanged.

binding_assumptions.name: Shared motion predicate within seasonal cause
binding_assumptions.content: C02 uses the one written MOTION24 constructor for both the source wheel-motion reference mu(W23,e) and the causally affected part-motion mu(A(s)14,e). This is an explicit predicate-sharing/ellipsis construction; the two participant arguments are written WHEEL23 and PART14. BY25 relates these, with variation and adjustment. No hidden second motion word is claimed, and PART alone is not allowed to assert physical motion. This extra semantic application of one word is counted as grammar, not a per-occurrence new denotation.

binding_assumptions.name: Quantifier scope shared with month progression
binding_assumptions.content: EACH36 binds m across both C03’s equality/sign statement and C04’s same-month progression/period statement. The binder closes at the complete month-unit end40, despite physical interleaving. MONTH39 resumes that in-scope m; it is not a free variable leaked from a closed universal statement or a silently selected different month. This joint scope is a fitted construction. The month parameter belongs to the source-described calendar context; no rule across unmentioned calendars or leap-year systems is asserted. I,W and Z are global apparatus identities across this month quantification; EACH does not create a fresh clock or index per month.

symbolic_content_contract.entities: Persistent F,C,X,W,Z,I and water Wt; no pair of distinct source parts conflated.
symbolic_content_contract.mechanics: Normal operating episode e: Raise(Wt,F,e) is coupled to Down(C,e), Turn(C,X,e), Transmit(X,mu(W,e)) under the declared apparatus. No numerical speeds/displacements.
symbolic_content_contract.seasonal: A(s) part of Z varies in ordered extent across stated times; W motion causes that display adaptation for Hh and s. No numerical mapping, drive rate or duration law.
symbolic_content_contract.calendar: For every m in the source calendar context, BOTH C03 and C04 hold: S(m) part of Z and |H(S(m))|=|D(m)|; I’s Pm has local moves between distinct holes in H(S(m)), shows spaces(Hh), and completes whole T(m). No transition count or actuator chosen.
symbolic_content_contract.epistemic_status: These are source constraints under unconfirmed target meanings/grammar, not independently recovered manuscript facts; no execution or engineering validation.
symbolic_content_contract.case_scope: e ranges normal operating cases. C01/C02 share e within a case; seasons may select distinct cases of the same apparatus. Pm is a separate index-history object over a month, not automatically one of those wheel events.
